To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the protein composition of the model bacterium Rhodpirellula batalica is growth phase dependent, that the regulation of proteins involved in amino acid metabolism, the tricarboxilic acid cycle and the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway is growth phase dependent and that the regulation of several proteins involved in cell motility and cell surface properties is growth phase dependent.

the protein pattern of R. balticais strongly influenced by the growth phase and that the stationary phase is characterized by a downregulation in the tricarboxylate cycle and oxidative pentone phosphate pathway, a downregulatio of enzymes involved in amino-acid biosynthesis and upregulation of sigmaH.
the proteome of R. balticas changes significantly during growth in batch cultures, with the number and magnitude of protein abundance changes being highest during stationary phase.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
R. balticais a versatile micro-organism, capable of adapting to different environmental conditions.

the stationary growth phase is a period of adaptation to a changing environment and that the regulation of proteins is a complex process that involves the expression of proteins with diverse biological functions.
growth phase dependent changes in R. balticais protein abundance are not only a result of the physiological state of the cell, but also a response to the environmental conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
R. baltcia is an excellent model for the study of the physiology and biochemistry of a marine bacterium, and that 2D-DIGE is a powerful tool for studying the proteome of this organism.

the transition from exponential growth phase to stationary phase is accompanied by an upregulation and downregulation of a broad spectrum of proteins, with many proteins of unknown function being involved in this process.
growth phase dependent protein expression is a highly complex process in R. baltical, which is reflected in the large number of differentially regulated proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
2D DIGE can be used for a quantitative analysis of growth phase-dependent changes in the proteome of R. balticas.
the 2D DIGE technology is a powerful and reliable approach to study growth phase dependent regulation of proteins.

the growth phase dependent protein expression pattern is a very complex phenomenon, and it is not possible to predict the regulation of one single protein by looking at the regulation of other proteins.
